newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Tesco targets Ireland's Quinnsworth - papers.
newsitem.headline: Tesco targets Ireland's Quinnsworth - papers.

text.p: British supermarket giant Tesco is poised to buy the Quinnsworth Group, Ireland's biggest food retailer, in a deal expected to be worth more than 600 million Irish pounds, newspaper reports said on Thursday.

The deal, which would be the biggest takeover in the Irish grocery trade, would also include the Crazy Prices and Stewarts operations in Northern Ireland which are also owned by Associated British Foods, the reports said.
It would give Tesco a 26 percent share of the grocery market in the Republic of Ireland and a 30 percent share in Northern Ireland.
But the Financial Times reported on Thursday that the talks between Tesco and ABF had collapsed.
"Although it is possible the talks could resume, this is thought unlikely," the British newspaper said.
